draft_claims.text: JSON binding handles decoder errors by returning the error directly from json.API.NewDecoder.Decode when it fails (line 52-53 in source_id:1), and struct validation is performed separately after successful decoding via validate(obj) at line 55.
Struct validation is implemented in validate(obj) which checks if Validator == nil; if not nil, it calls Validator.ValidateStruct(obj).

The default validator ValidateStruct handles nil objects by returning nil (line 48-49 in source_id:7), dereferences pointers to structs recursively before validating the struct itself, and validates slices by iterating elements.
The global switch EnableDecoderUseNumber (default false) calls decoder.UseNumber() to unmarshal numbers as Number instead of float64.
The global switch EnableDecoderDisallowUnknownFields (default false) calls decoder.DisallowUnknownFields() to reject unknown fields during decoding.

The global switch EnableDecoderDisallowUnknownFields is not explicitly defined in the provided source evidence; its existence and default value are inferred from usage but cannot be confirmed as a supported claim without declaration.

results.question: What is the difference between stopping at class level and stopping within a property rule during validation?

result.answer:
Stopping at class level occurs when the validator loop in ValidateInternalAsync breaks after a property rule adds failures, controlled by ClassLevelCascadeMode [2].

Stopping within a property rule occurs when the loop in ValidateAsync breaks after a component adds failures, controlled by CascadeMode [1].

The class-level stopping behavior is explicitly checked against ClassLevelCascadeMode in ValidateInternalAsync after each rule execution [2].

The property-level stopping behavior is explicitly checked against CascadeMode in ValidateAsync after each component execution [1].
